recipes.name: Emily's Easy Sausage and Spicy Tomato Dip
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can diced tomatoes with mild green chilies, undrained
2 (8 ounce) packages cream cheese, room temperature

steps.text: Cook the sausage in a skillet over medium heat until evenly browned and no longer pink. Drain. Reduce heat to low, and stir in the tomatoes and cream cheese until evenly blended. Cook just until heated through. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Emily's Easy Sausage and Spicy Tomato Dip
raw_recipe.description: This zesty dip will satisfy football fans with its blend of breakfast sausage with cream cheese and tomatoes seasoned with chile peppers. Serve it warm with tortilla chips.

review.reviewBody: I love this dip served warm! I like to use the Rotel w/ cilantro and lime...gives it a little kick.

I halved the recipe. I used a 9.5 oz bag of Jimmy Dean turkey sausage crumbles (delicious and a time saver), a 10 oz can of Rotel tomatoes and 8 oz light cream cheese. I threw it all in the crockpot. What an easy and fast dip. Delicious! Noone would guess it took all of 1 minute to make! Will definitely make this again and again.

I can't find the original poster of this recipe, but I used 1 original roll of Jimmy Deans and one hot. I threw in a half a roll of original Tennessee Pride (only because commenters were suggesting that brand and I like my dishes meaty). Two cans of original Rotel, (one drained and one not) and one brick of Philadelphia cream cheese. It was my first time making this. It was for a Halloween party this past Saturday, I didn't get ANY for myself!!! My crockpot was completely empty. To make matters worse, I DOUBLED the recipe!! Lol

This dip is delicious! I add some jalapenos to spice it up, and if I need to stretch it, another package of cream cheese. Wonderful as is or with modifications. After cooking the sausage, I either microwave everything until melted and/or keep it in the crockpot. This will definitely be a regular.

This was amazing. I thought it was runny so I added 1 1/2C grated old cheddar cheese and it was perfect. I needed it spicer so I used hot Italian sausage and chopped up some pickled jalapenos. I am sure the recipe as is would have been wonderful too. Anyway it was a hit. This makes a lot which is wonderful, most dips have to be doubled I find.
Very tasty. I double it and used 1 regular pork sausage and one 1 pound hot. Served with crackers and chips. Kept it warm in a crockpot. Big office hit!
very good recipe! tasty, but not overly spicy (my two year old loved it) we used spicy sausage & added bell peppers & garlic. great with crackers or tortilla chips.

In order to make it more waistline friendly, I used Neufchatel cheese and andouille chicken sausage. I removed the casing from the chicken sausage and browned. I also added an extra can of Rotel. Try using the different types of Rotel flavors to give it a varying twist.

I've been making this for years. Even my picky 5 year old likes it. I brown the sausage and then put all the ingredients in the crock pot on low for a few hours until cheese is melted and its warm. Because we have children I don't make it too hot but I put a can of chilies in the bowl that the kids don't eat for an extra kick.

This dip was the first thing to empty at my work function today! Everyone loved it and asked for the recipe. I made it exactly per directions. It was mildly spicey..perfect for a large group. Next time I'm trying HOT sausage and HOT RoTel. I also made it the night before, refrigerated it and heated in the crock pot at work. Perfectly simple and easy!

Great base recipe... I modified it a bit... I added green onion, bell pepper and garlic while cooking the sausage. I used only one 8oz. cream cheese, and added about 1/2 cup sour cream and about 1/4 cup parmesan cheese... I threw in some jalapenos from a jar, and I used the "chili fixin" rotel...It was AMAZING!!! I brought home an empty dish!!!
One of my favorite dips to make! It's so easy and so delicious...and cheap! It could almost make a meal if you wanted it to. Just as good left over. We serve with tortilla chips.
Another great recipe. I love this. I use mild sausage and mild rotel to tone it down a little. Scoops are great to use with this recipe so you get scoop to eat with a chip.
It was delicious and I will definitely make again soon! Thank you for the recipe!
This is extremely addictive. You can change the level of spice easily with different sausage as well as different canned tomato with green chilies. Once you start eating, you just can't stop.
I followed the direction to the T, and it was very bland, even for my omnivorous husband. Wasn't worth the time. May use it as a base recipe, but will add a lot more flavor next time.

What a Wonderful Dip.....I LOVE it! I didn't make any subs, but I did make a couple adjustments. I had a 1/2 lb of pork sausage leftover from an earlier recipe so I didn't have a full lb.. So I only used 1 pkg of cream cheese but I did use the entire can of Rotel (Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies). This gave a great consistency that I liked. The heat was perfect for me, but if you like it spicier, just add some cayenne.
Used 8oz cream cheese, and 8oz shredded cheddar. Also added a little crushed red pepper and cayenne for more spice.
Just ok. Not enough kick for us.
Great recipe! I added a large tablespoon of diced jalapenos. It fit perfectly into my small slow cooker.
